title: Autorepair signature registry and playlet dispatch
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description:
Problem: Support engineers repeatedly perform a small set of deterministic remediation steps for common incidents (OOM evictions, kube-proxy flaps, stale cache shards). These are currently ad-hoc shell snippets in Slack and ad-hoc runbook pages, which leads to slower MTTR and inconsistent execution.

Goal: Ship a lightweight, auditable registry that maps compact "signatures" (error fingerprints + context) to curated, parameterized "playlets" (small, idempotent remediation scripts/tasks). The registry will power an automated dispatcher used by the operator console and CLI for safe, one-click remediation and for scheduled dry-run self-healing.

Proposed components:
- Signature registry (Postgres-backed + search index): stores signatures, match rules (regex, jsonpath, ML-hash), severity, and recommended playlets.
- Playlet templates: parameterized task templates (idempotent, idempotency_token support, retry policy) stored in a signed catalog with semantic versioning.
- Dispatcher: policy engine that evaluates matches, applies authorization rules (RBAC + require-approval flags), and enqueues playlets to the task runner. Includes a dry-run mode and simulated-execution sandbox.
- Safety & observability: execution-only sandboxes, automatic snapshot of target state before playlet run, telemetry events, rollback playlets, and audit log entries.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Deterministic vs ML matching: start with deterministic rules (regex/jsonpath) for precision; add a calibrated ML classifier later for fuzzy matches (separate flag).
- Registry schema: normalize frequently-updated fields (score, last_seen) to a fast KV to avoid hotPG hotspots; core metadata stays in Postgres.
- Execution safety: prefer simple playlets (finite steps, no interactive prompts). Complex remediations are surfaced as operator instructions rather than automated runs.

Progress so far:
- Prototype schema and ER diagram: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Autorepair+Signature+Registry (design draft v0.1).
- Playlet template DSL v0 landed in feature branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5821 (WIP).
- Small demo wired into staging console for kube-proxy flaps (dry-run only): recorded in dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/autorepair-demo?orgId=1

Open questions / blockers:
- Authorization model alignment with Private deployments: need SSO/RBAC mapping for customer-managed principals (security to review).
- Canonical snapshot mechanism for pre/post state: infra team preference (etcd snapshot vs custom collector).
- Playlet signing and version pinning for Dedicated customers (legal/enterprise requirement).

Testing & rollout plan:
1) Internal alpha: dry-run-only dispatcher + audit logs; test against historical incidents (replay infra).
2) Canary opt-in: teams can enable active dispatch on non-production clusters with require-approval=false for low-risk playlets.
3) Gradual enablement: roll to production with require-approval=true for high-risk actions and automated fallback for failures.

Metrics to track:
- Match precision/recall (by signature), false-positive rate for automated dispatches.
- MTTR delta for incidents with applicable playlets.
- Playlet failure rate and mean time to rollback.

Longer-term: integrate ML-suggestion for candidate signatures, support a templating language for complex orchestration (limited to safe primitives), and expose a curated marketplace of playlets for common infra vendors.
acceptance_criteria: Registry accepts signatures and returns matches within 100ms p50 for typical query load
Playlet templates are stored with immutability and signed versions
Dispatcher supports dry-run and real-run modes with RBAC enforcement
Audit logs record pre/post snapshots and operator identity for all executions
Integration test harness can replay 50 historical incidents and simulate dispatch decisions
